I farm 20 mu here in Quzhou, and I've been doing this since I was a teenager. My land splits into two parts. About 15 mu sits on my good flat ground where I do wheat in winter and maize in summer — that's how everyone around here farms. The other 5 mu I put to stevia because the company comes to buy the dry leaves and the price is better than grain, even though it takes more work.

For wheat this year, I'll plant Jimai 22 like last year — my neighbor got over 500 kg and mine was close. I buy the compound fertilizer 15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu before planting with the rotary tiller, then I topdress 15 kg of urea per mu in March when the wheat starts jointing. That comes out to around 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate 4 times from the well — once before winter, then jointing, heading, and grain filling. Spray 2 or 3 times for aphids and rust. Rotary tillage is enough, I don't plough every year because it costs too much diesel.

For maize after wheat, I use no-tillage — drill Zhengdan 958 right into the wheat stubble. This saves time and the soil stays moist. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting and 20 kg urea at big flare stage, so about 22 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium. Two irrigations usually, jointing and tasseling, unless the rain comes good. Two sprays for borer and armyworm.

Stevia is different — the buying company tells us what to do and I've learned over the years. It needs more nitrogen and more water. I ploughed that plot to break up the soil. I put on about 25 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, 12 kg potassium per mu, some of it as manure I buy from the chicken farm. Irrigate 5 or 6 times through summer because it gets cut twice and needs to regrow fast. Three sprays at least — the leaves must be clean for the buyer.

I'd rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than end up short — a bad harvest hurts much more than an extra bag of urea. My wife and I handle most of the work, my older son works in Handan so I hire a couple of neighbors at wheat and maize harvest.
